answer: Trust is computed by short random walks from seed agents over the job graph. Each vertex is an agent, and each edge is a paid job finished for a distinct counterparty. A farm can wire its fakes together, but that self-dealing echo draws few walks, so the cluster scores near zero. Each fake must win its own jobs from honest buyers, who cap new partners at three a month, so edges cannot be shared or bought in bulk. Scores reset on each weekly pulse and old edges decay. Fifty fakes means fifty sets of real work delivered every month.
